body:
Investigate the randomized-corruption Dial timeout observed by journal PR #45's Linux Go 1.27 race job with GSO disabled. [Failed job](https://github.com/the-sarge/quic-go-fast/actions/runs/34164019896/job/101871388996).

At journal head `f71fd017a9e7e9624c1b43c6f5d66246aa304e0a`, `TestMITCorruptPackets/towards_the_client` failed with `context deadline exceeded` at `integrationtests/self/mitm_test.go:218`. The test uses real UDP/proxy timing; the Dial context at line 215 uses a scaled one-second deadline, three seconds in this CI run. The failure is not a race-detector report. Random corruption is applied at the existing callback around line 173.

The same test/assertion timeout was already observed on an unchanged pre-E3 baseline, as recorded in the [E1 receipt](https://github.com/the-sarge/quic-go-fast/blob/f271602adabd73520e5f92c04066970a3e7bb1e3/docs/audits/e1-emission-four-core/README.md#native-build-and-allocation-checks). This supports a pre-existing observation, not a demonstrated cause, identical semantic root, or proof that E3 cannot contribute. The current test/helper remains at merged source `f271602adabd73520e5f92c04066970a3e7bb1e3`, `integrationtests/self/mitm_test.go:215` and `:218`.

E3's product head passed its own required certification and hosted checks before merging. Journal PR #45 changes only an EOF append in `docs/DEV-JOURNAL.md`; no Go/test/module/workflow files differ from the merged product tree, and code/workflows do not consume this journal. The runtime check remains failed and was not rerun. Under the repository's explicit docs/runtime applicability rule it does not block this append-only documentation change.

Triage should establish a discriminating cause and finite next investigation before another random campaign. Preserve corruption, timeout and transfer behavior; do not extend deadlines or rerun until green without a separately accepted decision. This issue authorizes tracking only. It is separate from #44's simulated packet-loss accept/read/close timeout; sharing timeout wording is not a repeated-root argument.

comments.body:
Another matching observation occurred during H3 PR #142 local validation on macOS arm64 / Go 1.27.0. `go test -count=1 ./...` failed in `TestMITCorruptPackets/towards_the_client` at `integrationtests/self/mitm_test.go:218`: `context deadline exceeded` from `clientTr.Dial`, after the unscaled one-second context at line 215. This was a normal local run, without the race detector.

The tested working tree was subsequently committed unchanged as `f0ca437f638bc75f702f1fb8218942dfebaa2f58`, based on `45954f54fcca3a6906ea3a0c3b0a11f2b2aad56c`. Its only changes are `http3/exchange_test.go` and two plan/status documents; the MITM fixture and all production code are unchanged. HTTP/3 and the other packages passed. The observed test, assertion location and Dial error match this issue; an identical underlying cause has not been established.

```text
--- FAIL: TestMITCorruptPackets (1.17s)
    --- FAIL: TestMITCorruptPackets/towards_the_client (1.00s)
        mitm_test.go:218: Received unexpected error: context deadline exceeded
```

The operator explicitly directed that this failure remain separate from H3 after being told that H3 would need an exception to its passing-check requirement. H3 will continue review and remaining certification with this failed local check disclosed; this does not resolve #46 or authorize changing corruption/deadline behavior. No random repetition campaign, deadline extension or rerun-until-green was performed. Independently triggered push/PR hosted checks on H3’s unchanged head have all succeeded. No new architecture handoff is needed merely to record this recurrence; investigation remains here.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug

**Summary:** Investigate the intermittent client-directed corruption Dial timeout under a fixed diagnostic budget, and deliver evidence supporting a cause and proposed fix or a precise unresolved result.

**Readiness and authorization:** The maintainer completed triage and accepted an agent-ready investigation on 2026-09-09. This brief advances the issue's original tracking-only scope to the bounded diagnostic work below. `ready-for-agent` authorizes investigation, not an assumed fix or a requirement to make the test pass. No additional triage session is required before starting this brief. Production behavior changes, relaxed test behavior, and additional execution budgets require a subsequent maintainer decision.

**Current behavior and verification:**

`TestMITCorruptPackets/towards_the_client` intermittently returns `context deadline exceeded` from `Transport.Dial` before the shared MITM helper reaches accept or stream transfer. The [original Linux Go 1.27 race job with GSO disabled](https://github.com/the-sarge/quic-go-fast/actions/runs/34164019896/job/101871388996) records the failure after three seconds with `TIMESCALE_FACTOR=3`; triage inspected that log directly. The [E1 baseline receipt](https://github.com/the-sarge/quic-go-fast/blob/f271602adabd73520e5f92c04066970a3e7bb1e3/docs/audits/e1-emission-four-core/README.md#native-build-and-allocation-checks) records a matching pre-E3 baseline symptom. The [macOS arm64 Go 1.27.0 recurrence](https://github.com/the-sarge/quic-go-fast/issues/46#issuecomment-5605125412) occurred without the race detector. These observations do not establish an identical cause or isolate a regression. Triage verified the historical symptom and current code path, but did not perform a fresh reproduction.

At inspected source `901f53e0fcc8e8e5ff004de4f84a78728a61a150`, `testMITMCorruptPackets` selects datagrams using global `math/rand/v2` choices, replaces a randomly selected byte, sends the replacement directly through the endpoint transport, and returns true to suppress normal proxy forwarding. The callback ignores replacement-write results. Its long-header selection probability is 25%, despite a comment saying 20%; short-header selection is 5%. A selected replacement byte can equal the original byte. These are observations to preserve and investigate, not proven causes or permission to change the distribution.

**Desired outcome:**

Produce a diagnostic report that separates observations from hypotheses and distinguishes, as evidence allows, handshake delay caused by the corruption sequence, failed replacement writes or proxy behavior, and transport recovery failure. A demonstrated mechanism in a constructed case is not automatically the cause of a historical occurrence whose random choices were not retained. Completion may be inconclusive; passing attempts do not resolve the issue.

**Key interfaces and evidence requirements:**

- `testMITMCorruptPackets` and `runMITMTest`: preserve direction selection, byte-replacement behavior, direct-send/drop behavior, delay, scaled Dial deadline, and transfer assertions. Diagnostic capture must retain each corruption decision, direction, datagram order/length, byte offset and old/new byte, timing, and replacement-write result. Avoid additional random draws on the behavior path.
- `quicproxy.Proxy` and `DropCallback`: distinguish a UDP datagram from its possibly coalesced QUIC packets; account for normal forwarding versus direct replacement delivery and their timing/address differences.
- `Transport.Dial` and handshake/recovery tracing: correlate client/server handshake progress, packet drops, acknowledgments, loss/PTO events, and context expiry using existing tracing facilities where possible. Do not invent events absent from the evidence.
- Diagnostic replay, if needed, must identify the retained corruption schedule and the limits of reproducing live UDP timing, packetization, and cryptographic bytes. A test-shuffle seed alone does not reproduce the corruption choices.

**Bounded execution contract:**

1. Start with existing logs, receipts, source, and available traces. Pin the investigation revision and record relevant differences from the observed revisions. Write a short hypothesis table identifying evidence that would support or contradict each hypothesis before executing diagnostic cases.
2. Temporary local instrumentation and focused diagnostic fixtures are allowed in the investigator's own feature-branch worktree. Preserve the tested behavior, disclose timing effects from instrumentation, and retain the patch with the report. This does not authorize shipping a production fix.
3. Allow at most **four instrumented executions of the failing subtest**, at most two in each of the reported environments: Linux Go 1.27 with race, GSO disabled, and scale factor 3; macOS arm64 Go 1.27 without race and scale factor 1. Before each execution, specify the unresolved hypothesis and evidence to capture. Stop these fresh random executions on the first captured matching timeout. If an environment is unavailable, report that limitation; do not transfer its allocation to another environment. Do not reprovision infrastructure as part of this task.
4. Allow at most **eight additional focused executions total** for retained-schedule replay, deterministic mechanism probes, or matched controls. Each must have a predeclared discriminating hypothesis and expected observations. No fresh random campaign belongs in this allocation. Diagnostic execution attempts count regardless of result; build-only commands do not. No full-suite runs, CI reruns, or reset of the budget by changing revision, seed, instrumentation, or platform.
5. Stop earlier when a supported explanation and proposed next action are available. At budget exhaustion, stop and report the remaining uncertainty and the smallest evidence-producing follow-up. A proposed extension must state its exact budget and discriminating purpose; do not execute it without a new decision.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] A durable report records pinned source, instrumentation, commands, toolchains, platforms, environment settings, outcomes, raw evidence locations, and budget usage, including missing environments or artifacts.
- [ ] The report states whether a matching timeout was freshly reproduced and whether the evidence supports a historical cause, only a possible mechanism, or an unresolved hypothesis.
- [ ] Every executed diagnostic case is connected to a hypothesis and interpreted regardless of success or failure; passing runs are not substituted for failed evidence.
- [ ] The report provides either a supported cause with a narrowly scoped proposed fix and regression-test contract, or explicit unresolved alternatives with a finite proposed next experiment and stopping rule.
- [ ] Corruption, deadlines, transfer behavior, and public/wire contracts remain unchanged. Temporary instrumentation and its observer effects are disclosed.
- [ ] Publish the investigation result on this issue with durable evidence links and the required AI triage disclaimer. Leave the issue open unless a later accepted resolution actually resolves it. Do not send it through triage again merely because the result is inconclusive; request only the concrete next decision that the evidence requires.

**Redundancy and prior decisions:** Triage checked the corruption helper, proxy callbacks, handshake-loss fixtures, Dial cancellation, tracing helpers, and relevant compatibility/emission ADRs. No existing resolution or corruption-schedule replay facility was found in those surfaces. No `.out-of-scope/` knowledge base exists at the inspected revision. Preserve upstream public and wire compatibility and the accepted recovery-registration ownership contract.

**Out of scope:** Deadline extensions; changing corruption probabilities or suppressing handshake corruption; weakening assertions; skipping/quarantining the test; rerunning until green; production fixes or merges; new architecture programs; treating #44 as the same root cause; reopening E3 or H3 acceptance decisions solely on matching timeout wording.

title: Investigate intermittent randomized-corruption Dial timeout
